svg.title: PAR at a glance: from expert criteria to interpretable rewards
svg.desc: A fictional dialogue edit demonstrates the handbook as a system prompt, task-specific atomic questions, ordered binary answers, normalized token probabilities, and agreement with an illustrative human diagnosis. All images, answers, and probabilities are illustrative, not experiment outputs.

text.tspan: PAR AT A GLANCE / ONE TASK, EXPLICIT CHECKS, EXPLAINABLE FEEDBACK
Define what matters. Ask precisely. Verify each requirement.
Fictional dialogue edit · newly drawn media · illustrative answers and probabilities
Change “Meet me at noon” to “Meet me at dusk,” and “I’ll bring lunch” to “I’ll bring a lantern.”
Keep both speakers’ lips synchronized and preserve dialogue outside this exchange.
Atomic questions, grounded in the instruction
s = p(1) / [p(1) + p(0)] · p(1), p(0): next-token probabilities at each answer position
1 = requirement satisfied; 0 = not satisfied · Human column: illustrative expert labels
Does the first speaker now say “Meet me at dusk”?
Does the reply now say “I’ll bring a lantern”?
Are the first speaker’s lips synchronized with the new
Are the second speaker’s lips synchronized with the new
Is dialogue outside the edited exchange preserved?
Dialogue: correct. Lip synchronization: wrong. The failing requirements are explicit.
